records.label: 20 infants with LOPD diagnosed by newborn screening

variants.as_reported: IVS1 splice site variant c.-32-13 T > G

quotes: Of the 20 infants, four were homozygous for the "late-onset" IVS1 splice site variant c.-32-13 T > G, fourteen were compound heterozygous, and two did not have any copies of this variant.
Biomarker testing showed an increase in CK, AST, and ALT in 8 patients (40%) and increase in Glc4 in two patients (10%). All patients demonstrated postural and kinematic concerns.
Speech-language pathology assessments were normal in all patients and mild feeding/swallowing abnormalities were noted in nine patients (45%).

notes.statement: Huggins et al. (2022) found high variability among children with LOPD diagnosed via newborn screening. None of 20 infants had cardiomyopathy, but all showed postural and kinematic concerns, and the authors concluded that careful physical therapy evaluation is necessary to monitor for subtle musculoskeletal signs that may reflect early muscle involvement.
quotes: Our data show high variability among children with LOPD diagnosed via NBS. Careful physical therapy evaluation is necessary to monitor for subtle musculoskeletal signs that may reflect early muscle involvement.

notes.statement: Jones et al. (2021) assessed tongue structure and function by manual and quantitative muscle testing and ultrasound in 10 untreated LOPD patients, 30 patients with other acquired/hereditary myopathies, and 30 neuropathic controls. LOPD patients had significantly lower quantitative tongue strength and sonographic tongue thickness than patients with other myopathies. The authors concluded that quantitative tongue weakness and/or atrophy may help distinguish LOPD from other myopathies.
quotes: Greater tongue involvement was observed in LOPD subjects compared to those with other acquired/hereditary myopathies, based on statistically significant decreases in quantitative tongue strength and sonographic muscle thickness.
Findings of quantitative tongue weakness and/or atrophy may aid differentiation of LOPD from other acquired/hereditary myopathies.

notes.statement: Jones et al. (2021) found ultrasound to be an effective, efficient imaging method for quantitative assessment of the tongue muscles at the point of care.
quotes: our experiences in this study reveal US to be an effective, efficient imaging modality to allow quantitative assessment of the lingual musculature at the point of care.

notes.statement: Korlimarla et al. (2020) used brain MRI to study 14 children aged 6 to 18 years with Pompe disease who were receiving enzyme replacement therapy. They quantified white matter hyperintense foci with a summed Fazekas scale score. Ten of 12 children with infantile Pompe disease had mild to severe white matter hyperintense foci, with total scores of 2 to 23. The 2 children with late-onset disease had no such foci and scored high on most developmental assessments.
quotes: Mild to severe WM hyperintense foci were seen in 10/12 children with IPD (median age 10.6 years) with total FS scores ranging from 2 to 23.
The 2 children with LOPD had no WM hyperintense foci, and high scores on most developmental assessments.

notes.statement: Herbert et al. (2019) found that 4 of 84 patients (4.8%) with late-onset Pompe disease and the c.-32-13T>G GAA variant followed at their center were clinically diagnosed with symptom onset in the first 2 years of life (10 days to 20 months). Initial symptoms included delayed gross motor milestones, proximal weakness, swallowing and feeding difficulties, and sleep apnea; despite ERT all had residual muscle weakness.
quotes: Four patients out of 84 (4.8%) with LOPD and the c.-32–13 T > G variant, two males and two females, were diagnosed clinically and identified with early-onset symptoms.

The most common symptoms of early disease onset were delayed achievement of motor milestones with characteristic patterns of posture and movement reflecting weakness typical of Pompe disease (4/4), feeding difficulty (2/4) and sleep apnea (2/4).

notes.statement: Herbert et al. (2019) noted that the c.525delT and c.1827delC variants found in 2 of their early-onset patients were each present in 12 other patients in their LOPD cohort (24/83), all with adult-onset disease, suggesting that these genotype combinations with c.-32-13T>G are insufficient to cause the early-onset phenotype. ACE D/D genotype was not present in the 2 patients tested.
quotes: Two of these variants, namely the c.525delT and c.1827delC, were present in 12 patients each (totally 24/83; 28.9%) in our LOPD cohort, all of who had disease-onset in adulthood, suggesting that the presence of these particular non-IVS/IVS1 genotype combinations are insufficient to cause the early-onset phenotype.
Patients 1 and 4, whose ACE genotypes were available, did not have the unfavorable D/D alleles eliminating this as a likely reason for early onset.

notes.statement: Herbert et al. (2019) observed that all 4 early-onset patients improved on standardized motor assessments after starting ERT but remained below age level, with persistent weakness even at 40 mg/kg/week in 1 patient; antibody titers remained low in the 3 patients tested, so residual deficits were not attributed to high antibody titers.
quotes: all patients were functioning below age level before initiation of ERT and remained below age level on ERT, but all showed improvement after starting on ERT.

It is important to note that antibody titers remained low in the three out of four patients in whom titers were tested, which underscores the fact that the clinical decline and residual muscle deficits observed in these patients is not due to the presence of high antibody titers.

notes.statement: Forsha et al. (2011) evaluated baseline ECGs and echocardiograms in 87 adults with late-onset Pompe disease enrolled in a randomized trial of enzyme replacement therapy. Forty-six percent had one or more abnormalities, most often LVH by ECG (12%), short PR interval (10%), and decreased ejection fraction (7%); only 5% had elevated left ventricular mass index on echocardiogram, all mild, and the severe ventricular hypertrophy typical of infantile Pompe disease was not seen. The authors noted the abnormalities might be due to Pompe disease or to comorbid conditions.
quotes: Overall, 46% of patients had one or more of the ECG or echocardiographic abnormalities listed in Table 2 at baseline.

Although some patients with late-onset Pompe disease had abnormalities on baseline electrocardiogram or echocardiogram, those classically seen in infantile Pompe disease, such as significant ventricular hypertrophy, were not noted.
The cardiovascular abnormalities identified may be related to Pompe disease or other comorbid conditions.

notes.statement: Forsha et al. (2011) found that LVH by ECG criteria was not specific for increased left ventricular mass in late-onset Pompe disease. Of 10 patients with LVH on ECG, only 1 had an elevated left ventricular mass index on echocardiography.
quotes: Of note, in the 10 patients (12%) with left ventricular hypertrophy on ECG, only one had elevated left ventricular mass index on echocardiography (although two others did not have a baseline echocardiogram).
Data from our study suggest that left ventricular hypertrophy as assessed by ECG is not specific for the diagnosis of increased left ventricular mass in patients with late onset Pompe disease.

notes.statement: In a post hoc analysis of a 78-week double-blind trial that randomized patients 2:1 to recombinant human acid alpha-glucosidase (20 mg/kg every 2 weeks) or placebo, Forsha et al. (2011) found that ECG and echocardiographic parameters did not change significantly with enzyme replacement therapy and that there were no significant cardiovascular safety concerns. One patient with known Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome had an episode of supraventricular tachycardia that was classified as possibly related to treatment.
quotes: No significant changes in ECG or echocardiographic parameters were seen in association with enzyme replacement therapy compared with placebo.

a 40 year old male in the treatment arm with a known history of Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome and recurrent episodes of supraventricular tachycardia experienced an episode of supraventricular tachycardia 8 days after the week 6 treatment.
The Data Safety Monitoring Board classified this event as serious and possibly related to the study medication.

notes.statement: Forsha et al. (2011) found no significant difference in the frequency of cardiovascular abnormalities between patients with disease duration of less than 15 years and those with 15 years or more. Three (60%) of the patients whose symptoms began before 10 years of age had one or more ECG or echocardiographic abnormalities.
quotes: There were no significant differences seen in those with disease duration < 15 years vs. ≥ 15 years. Of note, in the patients who developed symptoms before 10 years of age, three (60%) had one or more ECG or echocardiographic abnormalities.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (2011) developed expert-opinion educational guidelines for an ACMG work group on several lysosomal storage diseases, including glycogen storage disease type II (Pompe disease). The guidelines cover confirmatory diagnostic testing and management of presymptomatic individuals found by newborn screening, family-based testing after a proband is identified, or carrier testing. The authors noted that the literature evidence was limited, so the recommendations had to be considered expert opinion.
quotes: Guidelines were developed for Fabry, Gaucher, and Niemann-Pick A/B diseases, glycogen storage type II (Pompe disease), globoid cell leukodystrophy (Krabbe disease), metachromatic leukodystrophy, and mucopolysaccharidoses types I, II, and VI.
the evidence in the literature is limited and consequently the recommendations must be considered as expert opinion

notes.statement: In 38 patients with late-onset Pompe disease, de Filippi et al. (2010) found that the ACE insertion/deletion polymorphism was distributed as in the general population (16% II, 37% DD). The DD genotype was associated with earlier onset of disease, higher creatine kinase levels at diagnosis, presence of muscle pain, and a more severe rate of disease progression, suggesting a potential role of the ACE polymorphism in modulating the phenotype and prognosis.
quotes: The distribution of angiotensin-converting enzyme polymorphism was in line with the general population, with 16% of patients carrying the II genotype, 37% carrying the DD genotype, and the remaining patients with the ID genotype.

The DD polymorphism was associated with earlier onset of disease (P = 0.041), higher creatine kinase levels at diagnosis (P = 0.024), presence of muscle pain (P = 0.014), and more severe rate of disease progression (P = 0.037, analysis of variance test for interaction).
These findings suggest a potential role of angiotensin-converting enzyme polymorphism in modulating Pompe disease phenotype and prognosis.

notes.statement: de Filippi et al. (2010) found that the three ACE genotype groups did not differ in mean age, disease duration, Walton score, or other disease severity scores.
quotes: The three groups did not differ in mean age, disease duration, Walton score, and other scores used to measure disease severity.

notes.statement: Bembi et al. (2008) noted that a clinical diagnosis of glycogenosis type II is confirmed by GAA enzyme activity in blood samples, cultured fibroblasts or muscle biopsies. Activity is virtually absent in infants and markedly reduced in juveniles and adults. They also reviewed the use of muscle imaging to evaluate muscle pathology.
quotes: The clinical diagnosis of glycogenosis type II is confirmed by virtual absence (found in infants) and marked reduced activity (found in juveniles and adults) of GAA enzyme in blood samples, cultured fibroblasts, and muscle biopsies.
use of muscle imaging to evaluate muscle pathology is reviewed

notes.statement: Bembi et al. (2008) described glycogenosis type II as a progressive, debilitating and often fatal neuromuscular disorder. Its clinical phenotypes form a continuum that varies in which organs are involved, age at onset and severity.
quotes: It is a progressive, debilitating, and often fatal neuromuscular disorder that manifests as a continuum of clinical phenotypes, which vary with respect to organ involvement, age at onset, and severity.

notes.statement: Bembi et al. (2008) reviewed the management of glycogenosis type II, a multisystem disorder. They recommended a multidisciplinary team of specialists, covering cardiology, pulmonology, neuromuscular disease, rehabilitation, nutrition and genetic counseling. They also reviewed treatment, including emerging therapeutic options.
quotes: Glycogenosis type II is a multisystem disorder that requires management by a multidisciplinary team.
In addition, treatment of glycogenosis type II is reviewed with attention to emerging therapeutic options.

notes.statement: Kallwass et al. (2007) showed that a fluorometric assay of GAA activity in dried blood spots, which uses acarbose, a highly selective alpha-glucosidase inhibitor, to eliminate isoenzyme interference, efficiently detected late-onset Pompe disease patients. They noted that these patients are frequently misdiagnosed by conventional methods because of residual GAA activity in other tissue types.
quotes: We recently introduced a simple and reliable method to measure GAA activity in dried blood spots using Acarbose, a highly selective alpha-glucosidase inhibitor, to eliminate isoenzyme interference.
Here we demonstrate that this method efficiently detects late-onset Pompe patients who are frequently misdiagnosed by conventional methods due to residual GAA activity in other tissue types.

notes.statement: Groen et al. (2006) reported ptosis as a feature of late-onset glycogenosis type II.
quotes: Ptosis as a feature of late-onset glycogenosis type II.

notes.statement: Montalvo et al. (2006) performed complete molecular analysis of the GAA gene in 40 Italian patients with late-onset GSDII and identified 12 novel alleles. Missense mutations were functionally characterized by enzyme activity and protein processing in a human GAA-deficient cell line, splicing mutations were studied by RT-PCR and in silico analysis, and a complex allele carrying three different alterations in cis was identified.
quotes: Twelve novel alleles have been identified: missense mutations were functionally characterized by enzyme activity and protein processing in a human GAA-deficient cell line while splicing mutations were studied by RT-PCR and in silico analysis.
A complex allele was also identified carrying three different alterations in cis.

notes.statement: Montalvo et al. (2006) found that the c.-32-13T-G mutation was the most frequent GAA mutation in 40 Italian patients with late-onset GSDII, present in the compound heterozygous state in 85% of patients (allele frequency 42.3%), as in other Caucasian late-onset populations; it occurred with c.2237G-A (W746X) in 9 of the 40 patients.
quotes: The c.-32-13T > G was the most frequent mutation, present as compound heterozygote in 85% of the patients (allele frequency 42.3%), as described in other late onset GSDII Caucasian populations.
Interestingly, the c.-32-13T > G was associated with the c.2237G > A (p.W746X) in nine of the 40 patients.

notes.statement: Montalvo et al. (2006) discussed genotype-phenotype correlations in late-onset GSDII, with particular emphasis on the subgroup carrying the c.-32-13T-G/c.2237G-A genotype.
quotes: Genotype-phenotype correlations are discussed with particular emphasis on the subgroup carrying the c.-32-13T > G/c.2237G > A genotype.

notes.statement: Amartino et al. (2006) reported a family in which two clinical forms of glycogen storage disease type II occurred in two generations.
quotes: Two clinical forms of glycogen-storage disease type II in two generations of the same family.

notes.statement: In a questionnaire study of 255 children and adults with Pompe disease, Hagemans et al. (2005) found that disease severity was associated with disease duration and not with age. Earlier onset of the disease meant that patients became dependent on a wheelchair or ventilator earlier.
quotes: Disease severity was associated with disease duration and not with age; an early manifestation of the disease implied earlier wheelchair or ventilator dependency.

notes.statement: Hagemans et al. (2005) found that patients under 15 years of age included a subgroup whose disease was more severe and progressed faster. They concluded that these patients need closer follow-up and early intervention, before irreversible damage occurs.
quotes: The patient group under age 15 included a subgroup with a more severe and rapid course of the disease. They require more intensive follow-up and early intervention, before irreversible damage has occurred.

notes.statement: Lam et al. (2003) found that the asymptomatic 13-year-old brother of a Chinese proband with juvenile-onset GSDII was also compound heterozygous for the P361L and R437C GAA mutations. They concluded that intrafamilial phenotypic variation in juvenile-onset GSDII occurs across ethnic groups, and suggested that other genes contribute to the phenotypic variability of GSDII.
quotes: The asymptomatic 13-year-old brother of the proband is also a compound heterozygote of the two mutations.
These results confirm that intrafamilial phenotypic variation of juvenile-onset GSDII is ethnically diverse and suggest the contribution of other genes to the phenotypic variability of GSDII.

notes.statement: Laforêt et al. (2000) studied 21 unrelated French patients with juvenile and adult-onset acid maltase deficiency; 17 carried the IVS1-13T-G transversion in the GAA gene (1 homozygous), and both mutant alleles were identified in 10 cases, with 13 different GAA mutations detected.
quotes: All patients but one were compound heterozygotes, and 17 carried the IVS1 (-13T ---> G) transversion (one patient was homozygous for this mutation).
The two mutated alleles were identified in 10 cases, with 13 different mutations detected in the GAA gene.

notes.statement: Laforêt et al. (2000) found no clear correlation between the type of GAA mutation and phenotype in French patients with juvenile and adult-onset acid maltase deficiency, suggesting a complex physiopathology.
quotes: There was no clear correlation between the type of mutation and phenotype.
The absence of genotype-phenotype correlation suggests a complex physiopathology that requires further investigations.

notes.statement: Laforêt et al. (2000) reported that 18 of 21 patients with juvenile and adult-onset AMD had a similar clinical pattern of pelvic girdle weakness predominating in glutei and thigh adductors; although progressive weakness began in adulthood in all but one, 16 had mild nonprogressive muscular symptoms in childhood.
quotes: Eighteen patients had a similar clinical pattern with pelvic girdle muscle weakness predominating in glutei and thigh adductors.
presence of mild, nonprogressive muscular symptoms appearing during childhood was detected in 16 patients

notes.statement: In a study of 18 patients with adult-onset GSD II, Ausems et al. (1999) found that measuring acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA) activity in muscle and analyzing muscle tissue under the microscope appeared to add nothing when GAA activity in leukocytes was clearly deficient. They found that elevated creatine kinase was a sensitive marker of GSD II, and they formulated a diagnostic protocol.
quotes: Measurement of acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA) activity in muscle and histopathologic analysis of muscle tissue appeared to have no additional value when GAA activity in leukocytes was clearly deficient.
Our study showed that creatine kinase elevation is a sensitive marker of GSD II. A diagnostic protocol is formulated.

notes.statement: Martiniuk et al. (1998) estimated the carrier frequency for glycogen storage disease type II in New York. From it they estimated how many affected individuals are born with the disease.
quotes: Carrier frequency for glycogen storage disease type II in New York and estimates of affected individuals born with the disease.

notes.statement: Raben et al. (1998) generated mice homozygous for targeted disruption of the Gaa gene (6neo/6neo) that lacked enzyme activity and accumulated glycogen in cardiac and skeletal muscle lysosomes by 3 weeks of age, with markedly reduced mobility and strength by 3.5 weeks. The mice grew normally, reached adulthood, and remained fertile; as in the human adult disease, older mice accumulated glycogen in the diaphragm, and by 8-9 months they developed obvious muscle wasting and a weak, waddling gait.
quotes: mice homozygous for disruption of the acid alpha-glucosidase gene (6(neo)/6(neo)) lack enzyme activity and begin to accumulate glycogen in cardiac and skeletal muscle lysosomes by 3 weeks of age, with a progressive increase thereafter.

They grow normally, however, reach adulthood, remain fertile, and, as in the human adult disease, older mice accumulate glycogen in the diaphragm. By 8-9 months of age animals develop obvious muscle wasting and a weak, waddling gait.

notes.statement: Raben et al. (1998) found that a second model, mice with deletion of exon 6 (Delta6/Delta6), had unimpaired strength and mobility up to 6.5 months of age despite biochemical and pathologic changes indistinguishable from the 6neo/6neo mice. The authors suggested that the genetic background of the mouse strains contributed to the differences among the models.
quotes: in a second model, mutant mice with deletion of exon 6 (Delta6/Delta6), like the recently published acid alpha-glucosidase knockout with disruption of exon 13

have unimpaired strength and mobility (up to 6.5 months of age) despite indistinguishable biochemical and pathological changes. The genetic background of the mouse strains appears to contribute to the differences among the three models.

notes.statement: Bijvoet et al. (1998) generated a mouse model of GSDII by targeted disruption of the Gaa gene in embryonic stem cells. Homozygous knockout mice lacked Gaa mRNA and had virtually complete acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency. Glycogen-containing lysosomes were seen soon after birth in liver, heart, and skeletal muscle, and large focal glycogen deposits had formed by 13 weeks of age. Vacuolar spaces stained positive for acid phosphatase.
quotes: A mouse model of this disease was obtained by targeted disruption of the murine acid alpha-glucosidase gene (Gaa) in embryonic stem cells. Homozygous knockout mice (Gaa -/-) lack Gaa mRNA and have a virtually complete acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency.
Glycogen-containing lysosomes are detected soon after birth in liver, heart and skeletal muscle cells. By 13 weeks of age, large focal deposits of glycogen have formed.

notes.statement: Bijvoet et al. (1998) found that male and female Gaa knockout mice were fertile. At 9 months of age the mice still had no overt clinical symptoms, but the heart was typically enlarged and the electrocardiogram was abnormal.
quotes: Both male and female knockout mice are fertile and can be intercrossed to produce progeny.
Overt clinical symptoms are still absent, but the heart is typically enlarged and the electrocardiogram is abnormal.

notes.statement: Kroos et al. (1995) studied 121 patients with glycogen storage disease type II. They looked at how common three mutant alleles were and which clinical phenotypes went with them.
quotes: Glycogen storage disease type II: frequency of three common mutant alleles and their associated clinical phenotypes studied in 121 patients.

notes.statement: Wokke et al. (1995) found that all 16 patients from 11 families with adult-onset acid maltase deficiency were compound heterozygotes carrying the IVS1(-13T-G) transversion on one allele; the second allele carried deletion of T525 in exon 2 in 7 probands (64%) or a deletion of exon 18 in 1 proband (9%).
quotes: All patients were compound heterozygotes and carried the IVS1(-13T --> G) transversion on one allele; the second allele harbored either a deletion of a T at position 525 in exon 2 (7 probands, 64%) or a deletion of exon 18 (1 proband, 9%).

notes.statement: Wokke et al. (1995) found that worsening handicap was related to age and decreasing vital capacity to how long the patient had had symptoms. Respiratory insufficiency was never the first manifestation.
quotes: Deterioration of handicap was related to age, and decrease in vital capacity to duration of the symptomatic stage. Respiratory insufficiency was never the first manifestation.

notes.statement: Wokke et al. (1995) found that serum creatine kinase activity and alpha-glucosidase activity in peripheral blood cells or muscle were helpful for diagnosis but had no prognostic value.
quotes: The levels of activity of serum creatine kinase and of alpha-glucosidase in peripheral blood cells or muscle were helpful for the diagnosis, but did not have prognostic value.

notes.statement: Wokke et al. (1995) concluded that the adult form of acid maltase deficiency appears to be both clinically and genetically rather homogeneous. They proposed that reduced alpha-glucosidase activity is the final common pathway that destroys muscle fibers and causes muscle weakness to progress over years.
quotes: The adult form of acid maltase deficiency appears to be both clinically and genetically rather homogeneous; decrease of alpha-glucosidase activity is the final common pathway leading to destruction of muscle fibers and progression of muscle weakness over a period of years.

notes.statement: Francesconi and Auff (1982) reported cardiac arrhythmias in association with the adult form of type II glycogenosis.
quotes: Cardiac arrhythmias and the adult form of type II glycogenosis.

notes.statement: Sivak et al. (1981) reported a 51-year-old man with adult-onset acid maltase deficiency who presented with a 6-year history of progressive exertional dyspnea due to diaphragmatic paralysis, with only minimal limb weakness; electromyography suggested the diagnosis, which was confirmed by electron microscopic and biochemical studies of muscle biopsy.
quotes: A 51-year-old man presented with a six-year history of gradually progressive exertional dyspnea. His complaint was attributed to increasing age, but evaluation finally led to a diagnosis of diaphragmatic paralysis.
Electromyographic studies suggested a diagnosis of acid maltase deficiency, which was confirmed by electron microscopic and biochemical studies of muscle biopsy sections.

notes.statement: Sivak et al. (1981) found that exercise stress testing was necessary to define the limits of exercise tolerance in their patient with adult-onset acid maltase deficiency and diaphragmatic paralysis.
quotes: Exercise stress testing was necessary to define the limits of the patient's exercise tolerance.

notes.statement: Beratis et al. (1983) found extensive genetic heterogeneity in acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency, with molecular differences between the clinical forms and within both the infantile and adult forms. Of 9 infantile-form fibroblast strains, 8 were cross-reacting material (CRM)-negative and 1 was CRM-positive. Two adult-form strains had reduced enzyme protein in proportion to their reduced activity, whereas a third adult-form strain had activity in the infantile range and no detectable CRM.
quotes: Of nine fibroblast strains derived from patients with the infantile form of the disease, eight were crossreacting material (CRM)-negative and one CRM-positive.
Molecular differences were identified both between the clinical forms of the disease and within the infantile and the adult forms of acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency.

notes.statement: Beratis et al. (1983) found that fibroblasts with phenotype 2 of acid alpha-glucosidase, which is considered a normal variant, had less enzyme protein and a reduced ability to cleave glycogen, but normal catalytic activity toward maltose. The authors stated that it remains unknown whether the deficiency in homozygotes for isozyme 2 is enough to cause glycogen accumulation and a muscular dystrophy-like disease later in life.
quotes: Fibroblasts with phenotype 2 of acid alpha-glucosidase, considered a normal variant, showed a reduction both in the amount of enzyme protein and in the ability of the enzyme to cleave glycogen. However, the catalytic activity for maltose was normal.

It remains unknown whether or not the enzyme deficiency in homozygotes for isozyme 2 of acid alpha-glucosidase will be sufficient to cause glycogen accumulation and lead to the development of muscular dystrophy-like disease later in life.

notes.statement: Slonim et al. (1983) treated a child with acid maltase deficiency with a high-protein diet for 12 months. The weakness and wasting reversed, and muscle function, exercise tolerance, and growth improved.
quotes: To reduce this muscle catabolism, the patient was treated with a high-protein diet for 12 months. This has reversed the weakness and wasting, with improvement in muscle function, exercise tolerance, and growth.

notes.statement: Slonim et al. (1983) found that circulating branched chain amino acids fell rapidly after protein ingestion in a child with acid maltase deficiency. They suggested that increased net muscle protein catabolism may play a part in the pathogenesis of the disorder.
quotes: A rapid fall in circulating branched chain amino acids after protein ingestion in a child with AMD suggested that increased net muscle protein catabolism may play a part in the pathogenesis of this condition.

notes.statement: Matsuishi et al. (1984) considered nasal vocalization and an EMG finding of abnormal insertion voltage followed by pseudomyotonic discharge, together with delayed developmental milestones and mild generalized muscle weakness, to be characteristic diagnostic findings for the childhood form of acid maltase deficiency.
quotes: In addition to a delay in developmental milestones and mild generalized muscle weakness, nasal vocalization and an electromyographic finding of abnormal insertion voltage, followed by pseudomyotonic discharge, were assumed to be characteristic diagnostic findings for the childhood form of AMD.

notes.statement: Matsuishi et al. (1984) found that neutral maltase activity was highest in the muscle biopsy from the patient with the least severe weakness and suggested that this enzyme may play a role in reducing muscle involvement in childhood acid maltase deficiency.
quotes: Since the neutral maltase activity was highest in the muscle biopsy specimen from the patient with the least severe weakness, the enzyme may play a role in reducing muscle involvement.

notes.statement: Hudgson et al. (1968) described adult myopathy due to glycogen storage disease caused by acid maltase deficiency.
quotes: Adult myopathy from glycogen storage disease due to acid maltase deficiency.

notes.statement: Swaiman et al. (1968) reported a late-infantile form of acid maltase deficiency.
quotes: Late infantile acid maltase deficiency.

notes.statement: Engel (1970) described acid maltase deficiency in adults as a syndrome that can mimic muscular dystrophy or other myopathies.
quotes: Acid maltase deficiency in adults: studies in four cases of a syndrome which may mimic muscular dystrophy or other myopathies.

notes.statement: Angelini et al. (1972) reported abnormalities in fibroblasts cultured from patients with adult acid maltase deficiency.
quotes: Adult acid maltase deficiency. Abnormalities in fibroblasts cultured from patients.

notes.statement: Trend et al. (1985) found characteristic glycogen vacuoles in peripheral blood lymphocytes in all 5 adults with acid maltase deficiency, whereas muscle biopsy was characteristic in only 1 of 4 cases. The diagnosis was confirmed by enzyme assay in muscle and cultured fibroblasts.
quotes: In all patients characteristic glycogen vacuoles were seen in peripheral blood lymphocytes.
Muscle biopsy was characteristic in only 1 out of 4 cases and showed minimal or nonspecific features in 3. The diagnosis was confirmed by enzyme assay in muscle and cultured fibroblasts.

notes.statement: Trend et al. (1985) reported that long-term home ventilatory support (25 patient-years), using a rocking bed or intermittent positive pressure ventilation via tracheostomy, allowed all 5 patients to return to work, and their clinical condition remained stable.
quotes: Long-term domiciliary ventilatory support (25 patient-years) using a rocking bed or intermittent positive pressure respiration with a tracheostomy has allowed a return to work in all patients, with their clinical condition remaining stable.

notes.statement: Molho et al. (1987) concluded that the bilateral diaphragmatic paralysis in adult twin brothers appeared to be an isolated lesion of genetic origin. They detected no neuromuscular or thoracic disorder that could explain it over 4 years of follow-up.
quotes: It appears thus to be an isolated lesion of genetic origin.
No infectious, metabolic, degenerative or proliferative disorders of the neuromuscular system and no thoracic diseases which could explain this lesion were detected during four years of follow-up.

notes.statement: Makos et al. (1987) suggested that basilar artery aneurysm formation in their sibship may have been a consequence of alpha-glucosidase deficiency. At postmortem, they found PAS-positive, diastase-sensitive material accumulated in vascular smooth muscle. Glycogen deposition in vascular smooth muscle had previously been described in the disorder but had not been clinically significant.
quotes: Glycogen deposition in vascular smooth muscle has been demonstrated previously in alpha-glucosidase deficiency but has not been clinically significant.
Basilar artery aneurysm formation in this sibship may be a consequence of alpha-glucosidase deficiency.

notes.statement: Bashan et al. (1988) found muscle glycogen content of 4 to 17% wet weight in 18 Israeli patients with alpha-glucosidase deficiency. Muscle alpha-glucosidase activity was zero in 10 of 17 patients examined, and in the 7 with residual activity the highest value was 18% of normal.
quotes: Muscle glycogen content varied from 4 to 17% wet weight. Muscle alpha-glucosidase activity was zero in 10 of 17 patients examined. Among the seven patients in whom residual activity was present, the highest value was 18% of normal.

notes.statement: Bashan et al. (1988) found leukocyte alpha-glucosidase activity to be highly variable and concluded that leukocytes are unfit for enzymatic diagnosis of the disease. They also found marked heterogeneity in the pH profiles of muscle and leukocyte alpha-glucosidase activity.
quotes: Leukocyte alpha-glucosidase activity was highly variable, making this tissue unfit for enzymatic diagnosis of the disease. A marked heterogeneity was found in pH profiles of muscle and leukocyte alpha-glucosidase activity.

notes.statement: Bashan et al. (1988) noted a high prevalence of glycogen storage disease type II in the Arab population of Israel. All but 2 of their 18 patients were Palestinian Arabs; the other 2 were siblings from a Jewish Iraqi family.
quotes: All patients were Palestinian Arabs, with the exception of two siblings from a Jewish Iraqi family.
A high prevalence of the disease in the Arab population was noted.

notes.statement: Isaacs et al. (1986) tried several forms of therapy in an adult with acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency and reported a favorable response to a high-protein, low-carbohydrate diet.
quotes: placed on various forms of therapy with favourable response to a high protein, low carbohydrate diet

notes.statement: Margolis and Hill (1986) treated a 55-year-old man with adult acid maltase deficiency and severe ventilatory muscle weakness with a high-protein (1.6 g/kg), weight-reducing diet for 27 months, which was associated with striking improvement in respiratory function, including measures of ventilatory muscle strength and endurance. They suggested that high-protein dietary therapy may be useful in adults with AMD and respiratory insufficiency.
quotes: High-protein dietary therapy was associated with striking improvement in respiratory function, including measures of ventilatory muscle strength and endurance.
We suggest that high-protein dietary therapy may be useful in adults with AMD and respiratory insufficiency.

notes.statement: Margolis and Hill (1986) based their dietary approach on evidence suggesting that muscle catabolism may contribute to muscle weakness in acid maltase deficiency.
quotes: Because recent evidence suggests that muscle catabolism may contribute to muscle weakness in AMD

notes.statement: Byrne et al. (1986) reported a family in which 7 members over 3 generations had a cardioskeletal myopathy with lysosomal glycogen storage in skeletal and cardiac muscle. Acid maltase levels were normal. The authors noted that this syndrome was unusual among glycogenoses because it showed dominant inheritance, and that it was the third report of non-acid maltase deficient lysosomal glycogen storage disease.
quotes: This is the third report of non-acid maltase deficient lysosomal glycogen storage disease
This syndrome is unusual among glycogenoses in having a dominant inheritance pattern.

notes.statement: Kretzschmar et al. (1990) found by electron microscopy lysosomal and cytoplasmic free glycogen in smooth muscle cells of the intima of large cerebral arteries and in pericytes of arterioles and capillaries in a patient with late-onset acid maltase deficiency; glycogen accumulation was associated with severe cellular damage and necrosis, which they thought resulted in the formation of numerous small intracerebral aneurysms.
quotes: Electron microscopy revealed lysosomal and cytoplasmic free glycogen in smooth muscle cells in the intima of large cerebral arteries as well as in pericytes of arterioles and capillaries.
Accumulation of glycogen locally was associated with severe cellular damage and necrosis.

notes.statement: Davis et al. (1976) described a syndrome of alveolar hypoventilation in 8 patients with bilateral diaphragm paralysis or severe weakness, 7 of whom had a generalized neuromuscular disorder. Transdiaphragmatic pressure change during maximum inspiration was zero in 5 patients and 2 to 6 cm H2O in the others (normal greater than 25). Vital capacity typically fell by about half when patients lay down, and hypoventilation was worse when patients were supine or asleep.
quotes: Eight patients were studied in whom diaphragm weakness had been suggested by paradoxical (inward) movement of the abdominal wall on inspiration, of whom seven had evidence of a generalized neuromuscular disorder.
In five patients, deltaPDi was zero and in the others ranged from 2-6 cm H2O (normal greater than 25 cm H2O) indicating paralysis and severe weakness in the respective groups.
Alveolar hypoventilation was present in five patients when supine and in six when asleep

notes.statement: Davis et al. (1976) found that alveolar hypoventilation in patients with diaphragm paralysis was associated with disturbed sleep, morning headache, and daytime fatigue. Using a cuirass respirator at night relieved the symptoms. The authors noted that fluoroscopy of the diaphragm gave misleading results.
quotes: Alveolar hypoventilation was associated with disturbed sleep, morning headache and day-time fatigue. Symptomatic benefit was achieved by the use of a cuirass respirator at night.
Fluoroscopy of the diaphragm was found to give misleading results

notes.statement: Askanas et al. (1976) found that muscle cultured from the biopsy of a patient with adult-onset acid maltase deficiency had the same abnormalities as the biopsied muscle. These included acid phosphatase-positive vacuoles, glycogen stored in secondary lysosomes, undetectable acid maltase and raised acid phosphatase. The authors said this supported the idea that the disorder is a biochemically distinct primary myopathy.
quotes: Morphologically and biochemically, the newly grown fibers of the cultured muscle showed the same abnormalities as those of the biopsied muscle.
Cultured muscle fibers demonstrate the same morphologic and biochemical abnormalities characteristic of biopsied muscle, supporting the concept of a biochemically distinct primary myopathy in man.

notes.statement: Mehler and DiMauro (1977) used a sensitive fluorometric assay and found residual acid maltase activity in muscle from patients with late-onset acid maltase deficiency (mean 6.91%, range 2.4 to 12.2%). They did not find it in muscle from 3 patients with the infantile form. Electrophoresis, kinetic studies and subcellular fractionation indicated that the residual activity was lysosomal acid maltase and not a contaminating neutral maltase isozyme.
quotes: Residual acid maltase activity was found by a sensitive fluorometric assay in muscle biopsies from 15 patients with late-onset acid maltase deficiency (mean, 6.91 percent; range, 2.4 to 12.2) but not in biopsy or autopsy muscle from three patients with the infantile form.
Electrophoresis, kinetic characteristics, and subcellular fractionation indicated that the residual activity was lysosomal acid maltase and not a contaminating isozyme of neutral maltase.

notes.statement: Mehler and DiMauro (1977) found no correlation between the amount of residual acid maltase activity and either clinical severity or glycogen accumulation in late-onset acid maltase deficiency.
quotes: There was no correlation between the amount of residual acid maltase activity and the severity of the clinical picture or glycogen accumulation.

notes.statement: Mehler and DiMauro (1977) suggested that late-onset and infantile acid maltase deficiency are genetically distinct. Their reasons were that acid maltase activity was present in muscle, liver and, to a greater extent, leukocytes in the late-onset form but not the infantile form, and that the two forms did not occur in the same family.
quotes: The presence of acid maltase activity in muscle, liver, and, to a greater extent, leukocytes in late-onset but not infantile acid maltase deficiency and the failure of the two disease forms to occur in the same family suggest that they are genetically distinct.

notes.statement: Beratis et al. (1978) found that acid alpha-glucosidase purified from adult-form deficiency fibroblasts had the same pH optimum, Km, electrophoretic mobility, thermal denaturation, and inhibitor sensitivity as the normal enzyme. Immune complexes from the adult-form cells showed enzyme activity, but the amount of cross-reacting material (CRM) appeared to be significantly lower than normal.
quotes: The pH optimum; Michaelis constant; electrophoretic mobility in starch; thermal denaturation at pH 4.0 and 7.0; and inhibition by turanose, alpha-methylglucoside and trehalose were the same in purified enzyme from normal and mutant cells.
Enzyme activity was demonstrated in the immune complexes of the normal and adult acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency fibroblasts, but not of the infantile form.
The amount of CRM in the adult form appeared to be significantly less than in normal cells or cells from the infantile form.

notes.statement: Beratis et al. (1978) concluded that the infantile case resulted from a structural gene mutation producing a catalytically inactive, CRM-positive enzyme. In contrast, the mutation in the adult form appeared to reduce the amount of enzyme protein in the cells.
quotes: The findings indicate that this case of infantile acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency is the result of a structural gene mutation which causes the synthesis of a catalytically inactive (CRM-positive) enzyme protein.
It appears that in the adult form, the mutation causes a reduction in the amount of the enzyme protein present in the cells.
